core_idea: Replace each pile value by its 2-adic valuation, the position of its least significant set bit. The game's outcome is controlled by the minimum valuation: an odd minimum is winning, an even minimum with all valuations equal is losing, and an even minimum with mixed valuations allows an infinite draw-preserving strategy.
key_observations: A pile is playable exactly when its least significant set bit position is greater than 0; the game ends when all positions are 0.
If all piles have the same positive least-significant-bit position c, then any move decreases every pile's position to c-1.
The minimum least-significant-bit position m is the decisive invariant-like quantity for classifying positions.
When m is odd, choosing a pile attaining the minimum forces all piles to m-1, giving the opponent an even equal-minimum losing structure.
When m is even and all piles attain m, any move gives the opponent an odd equal state, so the current player loses.
When m is even but not all piles attain m, players can keep choosing piles above the minimum, preserving both a minimum pile and a larger pile, so neither player is forced to end the game.
Counting configurations becomes counting arrays by the exact minimum of lsb values and, separately, arrays where all values have the same exact even lsb.
reasoning_patterns: Project numeric game states onto a smaller invariant that captures legal moves and outcome-relevant behavior.
Classify impartial game positions by structural cases instead of computing Grundy values when the transition has strong regularity.
Analyze what a move does to extrema, especially the minimum, rather than tracking every value.
Identify equal-state collapse: when all components share a key value, one move transforms the whole state uniformly.
Separate winning, losing, and drawing positions by whether a player can force progress or preserve a nonterminal invariant indefinitely.
Count outcomes by fixing an exact minimum and subtracting configurations with a larger minimum.
Use complement counting for the remaining category after disjoint winning and losing cases are counted.
questions: What simplified feature of each value determines whether a move is legal?
Is there an extremal value that controls the whole state?
What happens when all components share the same key feature?
Can I classify positions by the parity or category of an invariant?
Can a player preserve a nonterminal structure forever?
Can I count configurations by fixing the exact minimum?
After counting the decisive cases, can the rest be obtained by complement?
